🚨 *GLOBAL POLICY TRIGGERS ALERT*
• *Source/Speaker:* Airbus
• *Announcement:* Airbus plans to increase its annual sourcing of components and services from India to USD 2 billion before 2030, up from the current USD 1.6 billion, and will work towards boosting the country's aviation ecosystem by strengthening local manufacturing, MRO infrastructure, and aviation training.
• *Market Stance:* 🟢 BULLISH

📊 *CONFIDENCE LEVEL:* HIGH \(90\% \- Explicit corporate announcement by Airbus outlining increased sourcing targets and strategic investments\)

🎯 *INDIAN MARKET IMPACT:*
• *Vulnerable Sectors:* None
• *Strategic Tailwinds:* Aviation, EMS (potential for electronic component sourcing), Metals/Auto (potential for raw materials like titanium and aluminum alloys), Infrastructure (MRO and manufacturing facilities development)
• *Expected FII Sentiment:* Net Inflows \(This corporate announcement from a major global player signals confidence in India's manufacturing and aerospace capabilities, attracting foreign investment and contributing to the 'China\+1' narrative\. The increased sourcing indicates a potential supply chain relocation or diversification towards India for Airbus components and raw materials, including advanced assemblies and digital avionics\. This positive corporate action supports a favorable macro environment for India\. There is no strengthening USD\/INR pressure or domestic tariff increases mentioned that would lead to outflows\.\)

💡 *TACTICAL ACTIONABLE OUTCOME:* Fund managers should consider overweighting Indian companies in the Aviation sector, particularly those involved in component manufacturing, MRO, aerospace services, and related raw material supply chains, anticipating increased demand and partnerships due to Airbus' expanded commitment to India\.
